claims.claim: Reviewers report controller support issues where Xbox controllers do not function properly without workarounds.

citations.review_text:
As of mid-2026, playing with an Xbox controller is not possible w/o jumping through hoops. Enabling/disabling Steam input does not fix the issue. Enabling Steam input leads to multiple actions per button (pressing A to jump also opens the in-game camera, for example), and when Steam input is disabled, A scrolls one way while B scrolls another way (when they should be confirm and cancel buttons, respectively). 

Don't waste your time on this one unless you're a KB/M player, I guess.
Controller support not working for a game released on consoles. GG Ubisoft.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience performance issues on modern hardware, including low frame rates, stuttering, and crashing.

citations.review_text:
The game is very good, having in my opinion the best villain of the Far Cry series. BUT it's horrible having to use Ubisoft Connect just to start the game — you need an internet connection to launch the game even though it's single-player.

And finally, the performance - This game has a horrible performance with modern next-generation CPUs playing on ultra or medium, it only allows playing between 60 to 110 FPS, it being extremely rare to reach 100 FPS in most cases. There was already a situation in a mission in the arena where I went down to 40 FPS. The problem that even trying to play with the refresh rate changed to 60Hz (me having a 280Hz monitor) causes an insane input lag that becomes nauseating and unplayable. Needs an update to fix this.
extremley poor running. low fps on modern hardware, frequent crashing, stuttering etc. dont waste your money, i dont care how good the story is or whatever if i cant play it

claims.claim: Reviewers encounter issues with Ubisoft Connect failing to verify game ownership or asking for an activation key after previously working.

citations.review_text:
Far Cry 4 suddenly says I don't own the game I PAID FOR

I bought Far Cry 4 on Steam and put around 15 hours into it without any problems. I paid for the game, installed it through Steam, linked my Ubisoft account, and actually played it.

Now, for some reason, Ubisoft Connect has decided that I don't own the game anymore.

When I try to launch Far Cry 4, Ubisoft Connect asks me for an activation key / says it can't authenticate my ownership. The problem is that I bought the game on Steam, so I was never given some separate Ubisoft activation key to enter.

This is incredibly frustrating. I paid for this game and was able to play it for around 15 hours, and now the launcher is effectively telling me that my purchase doesn't exist.

And apparently I'm not the only person having this problem. There are multiple reports from other Far Cry 4 players experiencing the exact same Steam/Ubisoft Connect ownership issue.

I don't understand how a game I legitimately purchased through Steam can suddenly become "unowned" because Ubisoft Connect can't verify the license anymore. Steam clearly shows that I own the game.

Please fix the Steam ↔ Ubisoft Connect ownership/authentication issue instead of asking customers to purchase the game again or provide an activation key that they were never given.

I paid for Far Cry 4. I should be able to launch Far Cry 4.

Ubisoft/Steam support, please actually investigate the license/entitlement associated with my Steam purchase and restore access to the game I already paid for.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience technical issues on modern PC configurations, requiring players to restrict CPU affinity to physical cores to prevent crashes and stutters.

citations.review_text:
Far Cry 4 – Still Worth Playing

First of all, third-party launchers suck. 😭 Just let me launch the damn game from Steam.

I played this game back in my teenage years, but this time I actually completed it. Let's just say my previous version had a few... problems. 😂 The official version still has some technical issues, but at least I can actually finish the game.

But the game itself? I actually really enjoyed it. The story is good, and I love the Indian/Himalayan-inspired setting. It gives the game a different feel compared to the other Far Cry games. The Shangri-La missions were probably my favorite part. They were so different from the normal campaign and honestly looked beautiful.

I also really like that the campaign sometimes gives you the choice to kill or spare certain characters. But Ubisoft, why does the achievement just say “Decide ___’s fate”? 😭 Give us different achievements depending on what we choose! Something like RDR2 would have been so much better.
Also... this was probably the first game where I heard an NPC swearing at me in my own language. Getting verbally abused in Hindi by an NPC was an experience. 😂

Honestly, I only really like Far Cry 3 and Far Cry 4 in this franchise. But I don't know why Ubisoft loves making the same grindy, copy-paste, repetitive missions in basically every Far Cry game. 😭

And finally... this game is OLD. With newer hardware, I literally had to open Task Manager → Details → FarCry4.exe → Set Affinity → disable all processors → select specific cores just to get the damn game running.
And apparently I have to do that every time I launch it. 💀

Still, I had fun with it. The story, setting, and gameplay are good enough to make me come back.

⭐ 8/10 – Still one of my favorite Far Cry games. The setting, story, and Shangri-La made this trip back to Kyrat worth it.

4/5

There are way too many collectibles and secondary missions for the otherwise short campaign.
I gave up finishing this game, it just feels like a hassle at this point, which is a shame, because it was on my bucket list, to play through this game at least once. 

I'd rather reccomend playing Far Cry 5, that's the best Far Cry game in the frenchise for sure.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the open world as visually impressive with a detailed Himalayan setting, complemented by a variety of traversal tools like the wingsuit and gyrocopter.

citations.review_text: As my first entry into the franchise, Far Cry 4 made an great first impression with its stunning Himalayan setting, chaotic open-world sandbox, and a compelling narrative anchored by the antagonist. Traversing the map with wingsuit and liberating outposts offers great immersion and tactical freedom. However, this is occasionally undercut by repetitive side activities and hundreds of time-wasting collectibles. Overall, it is a fantastic gateway into the series if you just focus on the emergent open-world combat and skip the map bloat.

This is my first Far Cry game and I really enjoyed it after 80 hours of playing. 🎮

The story was better than I expected. You play as Ajay Ghale, who comes to Kyrat for a personal reason, but things quickly become much bigger. I really liked Pagan Min as a character. He is one of the most interesting parts of the game for me. I also liked the different characters and the choices you have during the story. I won't talk about the ending because I don't want to spoil it, but there were some moments that I will remember. 👑

Kyrat is probably my favorite part of the game. 🏔️ The map is huge and there is always something to do. You can explore, hunt, capture outposts, find new weapons or just drive around the map. The mountains, forests and snowy areas look beautiful. Going to the highest snowy areas and flying around with the glider was really fun. 🪂 I also enjoyed flying the helicopter and looking at Kyrat from above. 🚁

The combat is really fun too. 🔫 I especially liked stealth. Using the bow and knives to silently take out enemies was very satisfying. 🏹 But you can also use guns, grenades and grenade launchers if you want to play more aggressively. 💥 I really like that the game gives you freedom to choose how you want to approach each situation.

There are also a lot of weapons and you can customize them with different attachments. The weapon system reminded me a little of PUBG and Battlefield, which I liked. There are enough different weapons to make the gameplay feel fresh. 🔫

For a game from 2014, I think the graphics still look really good. 🎨 The mountains, snow, forests and sunsets are beautiful. The environment is probably one of the main reasons I enjoyed exploring the map so much.

The soundtrack is also really good. 🎵 It fits the world and the atmosphere very well. There is one song that especially stayed with me, The River. The moment when I heard it near the end of the game was really memorable. I won't say more because I don't want to spoil anything, but t…

Farcry 4 improves upon visuals and setting. Accesibility of areas are also improved via wing suit and mini heli vehicle. Sometimes the visuals are breathtaking. Rest is very good but not exceptional. Big brother of Far Cry 3 . For me, story felt like a side quest. You can enjoy your time here nonetheless.
